primary_citation: Cal. Civil Code §3294 (Stats. 1987, Ch. 1498, effective Jan. 1, 1988)
short_title: Civil Code §3294 — Punitive Damages: Malice, Oppression, and Fraud; Employer Liability
one_line_rule: Punitive damages require clear and convincing proof of malice, oppression, or fraud as defined by §3294(c); corporate employer liability requires advance knowledge, authorization/ratification, or personal guilt on the part of an officer, director, or managing agent.

evolution_chain.label: Field Code Codification — Common Law Terms, No Definitions

case_law.key_rule: Conscious disregard malice: prior pattern of known dangerous conduct + subjective awareness of high probability of injury + willingness to proceed = §3294 malice. Pattern evidence of prior incidents is admissible to establish subjective awareness.

case_law.court: Court of Appeal of California, First Appellate District
case_law.key_rule: Managing agent under §3294(b) means employee with substantial discretionary authority over decisions that determine corporate policy — not merely supervisory authority. Ratification by managing agent can occur post-conduct through knowing approval or acquiescence.

case_law.cite: College Hospital Inc. v. Superior Court, 8 Cal.4th 704 (1994)
case_law.key_rule: Defines 'despicable' conduct under the post-1987 §3294: conduct so vile, base, contemptible, miserable, wretched or loathsome that ordinary decent people would despise it. Both malice §3294(c)(1) and oppression §3294(c)(2) require this threshold. Also governs §425.13 / §3295 procedural sequence for healthcare defendants.

three_paths_to_corporate_liability: Advance knowledge of physician/staff unfitness (prior complaints, peer review findings) + conscious disregard = §3294(b)(1)
Medical director, department chair, or risk management decision to continue employing or credentialing after knowledge of misconduct = ratification by managing agent = §3294(b)(2)
Hospital policy or protocol itself constitutes malice/oppression/fraud = personally guilty path = §3294(b)(3)
medical_malpractice_application.spine_surgery_fraud_theory: If surgeon performed surgery with no genuine medical indication (fraud under §3294(c)(3)) and hospital credentialing/risk management knew or ratified, §3294 punitive damages available against both surgeon and hospital
medical_malpractice_application.sirva_theory: Provider who used improper injection technique after prior SIRVA outcomes = Taylor-pattern conscious disregard malice under §3294(c)(1) despicable + conscious disregard prong
medical_malpractice_application.financial_condition_discovery: §3295(a)-(b): before trial, punitive damages plaintiff may obtain discovery of defendant's financial condition only after court authorization on good cause showing; at trial, jury considers financial condition in determining punitive amount
medical_malpractice_application.clear_and_convincing_standard: Higher than preponderance; lower than reasonable doubt; jury must be 'firmly convinced' that clear and convincing evidence establishes malice/oppression/fraud
medical_malpractice_application.bifurcation: §3295(d): on defendant's motion, trial bifurcated: liability and compensatory damages tried first; if plaintiff prevails, financial condition evidence introduced in second phase
